policy: NVIDIA G1 tracker / new external heading feedback comparison
reference: Identical CMU07/04 fitted reference, moving initialization and physics. Reference skeleton is never aligned to hide drift.

protocol.feedback_definition: Using the fixed reference start-to-end course, compute cross-track position error and reference-minus-actual root lateral velocity. Desired yaw offset is atan2(position_gain*cross_track_error + velocity_gain*lateral_velocity_error, max(reference_forward_velocity, minimum_forward_speed)). Clamp to 25 degrees, low-pass with 0.15 s time constant, and rate-limit to 60 degrees/s. Apply the SAME world-up yaw offset by left multiplication to all four future torso quaternions. Hold that offset over the lookahead horizon; preserve relative future rotations. No joint, joint-velocity, contact, root or duration reference changes.
protocol.design_rationale: A one-second lateral position recovery time and unit velocity-error damping are interpretable outer-loop defaults, not fitted to a successful trial. The yaw/rate limits restrict this to modest steering; smoothing is comparable to the 0.16 s policy horizon. The frozen three-case scope permits no gain search.
protocol.comparison: Baseline and feedback use identical saved reference poses, initial pose/velocity, policy, physics, gains, timing and zero action history. Every original physical criterion remains in force. Also report reference-relative cross-track and along-track errors in a rigid-transform-invariant path frame; do not substitute these for the original gates.
protocol.scope: One reproduced baseline, one common-yaw/translation invariance rollout, and one new causal heading-feedback trial only after diagnosis passes. Static graph probes are counted separately. No post-initialization state assignment, external forces, policy training, source changes or threshold relaxation.

limitations: Heading feedback is new external control, not an achievement of the unmodified pretrained policy.
One frozen feedback trial; no gain search, start-from-rest result, generalization or SOTA claim.
All original physical gates remain. Both cases fail lateral drift, root tracking and body tracking.
Lateral/root tracking improves, but along-track lag and left-foot slip worsen.
Strict full-joint yaw-equivariance diagnostic failed; it remains failed, alongside the independent one-step resolution.
